newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMD says German PC makers to use K6 chip.
newsitem.headline: AMD says German PC makers to use K6 chip.

text.p: Computer chip maker Advanced Micro Devices Inc said on Thursday several German PC companies would agree to use the forthcoming AMD K6 processor early next month.
"There will be an announcement in Munich on April 4," Dirk Heinen, an AMD product manager, told Reuters at the CeBIT computer trade fair here.

Heinen declined to name the German companies that will use K6, an advanced chip that AMD hopes will enable it to compete with Pentium chips from Intel Corp. But many of the first K6 PCs would come from PC makers that sell mostly to consumers, not businesses.

Heinen also said four of the world's top 10 PC makers were interested in K6, which will be ready in the second quarter. "They might not use it right out the chute, but we think our chances are pretty good for later this year," he said.

K6 is a critical product for AMD. It suffered several quarterly losses in 1995 and 1996 after its K5 chip was hit by development delays. By the time K5 was ready, Intel had already produced still faster chips and few PC makers were interested.
Compaq Computer Corp had been planning to use K5 until the development debacle.

At CeBIT AMD was demonstrating a K6 chip running at 200 megaherz. That is the same speed as Intel's fastest processor, although Intel said its Pentium II chip would be ready in the second quarter at speeds well above 200 megahertz.

To drum up interest in K6, AMD at CeBIT said it would begin selling chipsets that let PC companies build computers using an AMD processor due shortly -- or processors from competitors Intel or Cyrix Corp.
The AMD-640 chip set is compatible with a socket that can accept a K6, Intel Pentium or Cyrix 6x86 chip, AMD Marketing Director Dana Krelle told a news conference.

Krelle predicted the type of socket the chip set supports -- called "socket 7" -- would be used for at least 50 million PCs per year through 2000, although that not mean all of those computers would use K6 processors.
Competing socket 7 chip sets are available from other semiconductor companies.
Intel has been working on a different type of socket that would force other chip makers to alter their processor design.
